arxiv-2110-01581.title: Quickest Change Detection with Non-Stationary Post-Change Observations
arxiv-2110-01581.creator: Yuchen Liang, Alexander G. Tartakovsky, Venugopal V. Veeravalli
arxiv-2110-01581.description: Abstract The problem of quickest detection of a change in the distribution of a sequence of independent observations is considered. The pre-change observations are assumed to be stationary with a known distribution, while the post-change observations are allowed to be non-stationary with some possible parametric uncertainty in their distribution.

arxiv-2310-12965.title: Pre-optimizing variational quantum eigensolvers with tensor networks
arxiv-2310-12965.creator: Abid Khan, Bryan K. Clark, Norm M. Tubman
arxiv-2310-12965.description: Abstract The variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) is a promising algorithm for demonstrating quantum advantage in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. However, optimizing VQE from random initial starting parameters is challenging due to a variety of issues including barren plateaus, optimization in the presence of noise, and slow convergence.

arxiv-2408-01280.title: Hydrodynamics of molecular rotors in lipid membranes
arxiv-2408-01280.creator: Vinny Chandran Suja, Naomi Oppenheimer, Howard A. Stone
arxiv-2408-01280.description: Abstract Molecular rotors form twisted conformations upon photoexcitation, with their fluorescence relaxation time serving as a measure of viscosity. They have been used to assess membrane viscosities but yield higher values compared to other methods. Here, we show that the rotor’s relaxation time is influenced by a combination of membrane viscosity and interleaflet friction.

arxiv-2408-06605.title: Wormhole Geometries Supported by Strange Quark Matter and Phantom-like Generalized Chaplygin gas within f ⁡ ( Q ) f(Q) Gravity
arxiv-2408-06605.creator: Sneha Pradhan, Zinnat Hassan, P.K. Sahoo
arxiv-2408-06605.description: Abstract A crucial aspect of wormhole (WH) physics is the inclusion of exotic matter, which requires violating the null energy condition. Here, we explore the potential for WHs to be sustained by quark matter under conditions of extreme density along with the phantom-like generalized cosmic Chaplygin gas (GCCG) in symmetric teleparallel gravity.

arxiv-2409-17358.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Michael Groechenig, Dimitri Wyss, Paul Ziegler. We study p p -adic manifolds associated with twisted points of quotient stacks 𝒳 = [ U / G ] \Xc=[U/G] and their quotient spaces π : 𝒳 → X \pi:\Xc\to X . We prove several structural results about the fibres of π \pi and derive in particular a formula expressing p p -adic integrals on X X in terms of the cyclotomic inertia stack of 𝒳 \Xc , generalizing the orbifold formula for Deligne-Mumford stacks.

arxiv-2506-01320.title: Ψ \Psi -Sampler: Initial Particle Sampling for SMC-Based Inference-Time Reward Alignment in Score Models
arxiv-2506-01320.creator: Taehoon Yoon Yunhong Min Kyeongmin Yeo Minhyuk Sung[0.2em] KAIST {taehoon,dbsghd363,aaaaa,mhsung}@kaist.ac.kr
arxiv-2506-01320.description: Abstract We introduce Ψ \Psi - Sampler , an SMC-based framework incorporating pCNL-based initial particle sampling for effective inference-time reward alignment with a score-based generative model. Inference-time reward alignment with score-based generative models has recently gained significant traction, following a broader paradigm shift from pre-training to post-training optimization.

arxiv-2507-01220.title: Probing aqueous interfaces with spin defects
arxiv-2507-01220.creator: Alfonso Castillo, Gustavo R. Pérez-Lemus, Mykyta Onizhuk, Giulia Galli
arxiv-2507-01220.description: Abstract Understanding the physical and chemical properties of aqueous interfaces is important in diverse fields of science, ranging from biology and chemistry to materials science. In spite of crucial progress in surface sensitive spectroscopic techniques over the past decades, the microscopic properties of aqueous interfaces remain difficult to measure.

arxiv-2510-02845.title: Plasmonic metamaterial time crystal
arxiv-2510-02845.creator: Tingwen Guo, Jules Sueiro, Gian Marcello Andolina, Artem Levchuk, Stefano Ponzoni, Romain Grasset, Donald Monthe, Ian Aupiais, Dmitri Daineka, Javier Briatico, Thales VAG de Oliveira, Alexey Ponomaryov, Atiqa Arshad, Arjun Karimbana-Kandy, Gulloo Lal Prajapati, Igor Ilyakov, Jan-Christoph Deinert, L
arxiv-2510-02845.description: Abstract Periodically driven optical materials and metamaterials have recently emerged as a promising platform for realizing photonic time crystals (PTCs)—systems whose optical properties are strongly and periodically modulated on time scales comparable to the optical cycle of light Asgari_2024 .

arxiv-2510-13999.title: REAP the Experts: Why Pruning Prevails for One-Shot MoE compression
arxiv-2510-13999.creator: Mike Lasby, Ivan Lazarevich, Nish Sinnadurai, Sean Lie, Yani Ioannou, Vithursan Thangarasa
arxiv-2510-13999.description: Abstract Sparsely-activated Mixture-of-Experts (SMoE) models offer efficient pre-training and low latency but their large parameter counts create significant memory overhead, motivating research into expert compression. Contrary to recent findings favouring expert merging on discriminative benchmarks, we demonstrate that expert pruning is a superior strategy for generative tasks.

arxiv-2511-08716.creator: Ce Sui, Yi Mao, Xiaosheng Zhao, Tao Jing, Benjamin D. Wandelt
arxiv-2511-08716.description: Abstract The advent of increasingly advanced surveys and cosmic tracers has motivated the development of new inference techniques and novel approaches to extracting information from cosmic fields. A central challenge in this endeavor is to quantify the information content carried by these summary statistics in cosmic fields.

arxiv-2601-08107.title: STO-RL: Offline RL under Sparse Rewards via LLM-Guided Subgoal Temporal Order
arxiv-2601-08107.creator: Chengyang Gu, Yuxin Pan, Hui Xiong, Yize Chen
arxiv-2601-08107.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Chengyang Gu, Yuxin Pan, Hui Xiong, Yize Chen. Offline reinforcement learning (RL) enables policy learning from pre-collected datasets, avoiding costly and risky online interactions, but it often struggles with long-horizon tasks involving sparse rewards. Existing goal-conditioned and hierarchical offline RL methods decompose such tasks and generate intermediate rewards to mitigate limitations of traditional offline RL, but usually overlook temporal dependencies among subgoals and rely on imprecise reward shaping, leading to suboptimal policies.

pmc-10534001.title: Deep learning classification of systemic sclerosis from multi-site photoplethysmography signals
pmc-10534001.creator: Sadaf Iqbal, Jaume Bacardit, Bridget Griffiths, John Allen
pmc-10534001.description: Introduction: A pilot study assessing a novel approach to identify patients with Systemic Sclerosis (SSc) using deep learning analysis of multi-site photoplethysmography (PPG) waveforms (“DL-PPG”). Methods: PPG recordings having baseline, unilateral arm pressure cuff occlusion and reactive hyperaemia flush phases from 6 body sites were studied in 51 Controls and 20 SSc patients.

pmc-11645931.title: P086 Taking a Comprehensive Approach to Investigating Screen Time and Sleep in Preschoolers With and Without Autism
pmc-11645931.creator: E Axelsson
pmc-11645931.description: Children’s screen time has increased, and the majority of children exceed recommended screen time limits. Relationships between screen time and development are reportedly mixed, but children who meet recommended guidelines for screen time, physical activity, and sleep, perform better on cognitive measures (Walsh et al., 2018).

pmc-11710750.title: Delivery of mRNA encoding an anti‐tau monoclonal antibody and engineered scFv intrabody results in functional antibody expression in neurons
pmc-11710750.creator: Patricia Wongsodirdjo, Alayna C Caruso, Alicia Yong, Madeleine Lester, Laura J Vella, Ya Hui Hung, Rebecca M Nisbet
pmc-11710750.description: BackgroundMonoclonal antibodies have emerged as a leading therapeutic agent for the treatment of disease, including Alzheimer’s disease. Such antibodies, however, are expensive and timely to produce and require frequent dosing regimens to ensure disease‐modifying effects. Synthetic in vitro‐transcribed mRNA encoding antibodies presents a promising alternative to conventional passive immunotherapy and overcomes the need to generate recombinant antibodies.

pmc-12005440.description: Epithelial cells transport substances through the cellular and paracellular pathways. The last one depends on tight junctions, particularly on claudins, the family of integral membrane proteins responsible for the permeability and selectivity of these junctions. 300 nM ouabain (OUA) induces endocytosis and lysosomal degradation of claudin-2 and -4 in an Src and ERK1/2 kinases-dependent manner.

pmc-13095686.title: Outpatient intravenous sedation for dental treatment in patients with special health care needs: a five-year retrospective study in Venezuela
pmc-13095686.creator: Mariana Morales-Chávez
pmc-13095686.description: BackgroundPatients with special health care needs (SHCN) frequently present behavioral and medical conditions that complicate conventional dental treatment. This study aimed to describe the clinical profile, dental procedures, pharmacological protocols, and safety outcomes of outpatient intravenous sedation in SHCN patients treated in a specialized center in Venezuela.

pmc-13116037.title: Adenosine A2A Receptors Control the Mis‐Localization of Aquaporin‐4 in Rats Subject to Repeated Restraint Stress
pmc-13116037.creator: Liliana Dias, Samira G Ferreira, Ana Margarida Nabais, Joana Silva, Rodrigo A Cunha, Paula Agostinho
pmc-13116037.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Repeated stress triggers anxiety accompanied by a deregulation of cortical glucocorticoid receptors, which is relieved by blocking adenosine A2A receptors (A2AR). A2AR also controls the glymphatic system and the polarization of its key driver aquaporin‐4 (AQP4). Since the glymphatic system is altered upon repeated stress, we now tested if A2AR blockade could alleviate AQP4 polarization in rats subject to repeated restraint stress (RRS).

pmc-13340850.title: Human neural stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles improve cognitive function following glioma chemoradiation therapy
pmc-13340850.creator: Casey Hudson, Robert P. Krattli, Sanad M. El-Khatib, Arya R. Vagadia, An H. Do, Shreya Madan, Manal T. Usmani, Tracy Nguyen, Devyani Swami, Katja M. Piltti, Leslie M. Thompson, Brian J. Cummings, Aileen J. Anderson, Munjal M. Acharya
pmc-13340850.description: Cranial radiation therapy (RT) with concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ; Stupp protocol) prolongs glioma survival but frequently results in persistent cognitive impairment. Human neural stem cell (hNSC)-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) are a promising acellular therapy whose bioactive cargo can modulate neuroinflammation and synaptic integrity.

pmc-13569901.title: Bringing the Reading Sciences Into the Classroom: Insights for Phonics Instruction
pmc-13569901.creator: Tobias Ungerer, Kathleen Rastle, Blair C Armstrong
pmc-13569901.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Teaching phonics—that is, systematic mappings between letters and sounds—plays a foundational role in how children learn to read in alphabetical writing systems. Although the reading sciences yield important insights into the factors underlying effective phonics instruction, these findings have not been sufficiently linked to key decisions that teachers must make in the classroom—for instance, which spelling-sound regularities to teach, in what order to introduce them, how to illustrate them with example words, and when to teach exception words.

uslaw-usc-t42-s9151.title: 42 U.S.C. § 9151 — Prohibited acts
uslaw-usc-t42-s9151.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s9151.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 99 (Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion); Subchapter III (Enforcement). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. It is unlawful for any person who is a United States citizen or national, or a foreign national in or on board an ocean thermal energy conversion facility or plantship or on board any vessel documented or numbered.
